evidence: Every allocation has one declared mutable owner, legal accessors, bounded byte ranges, and a release ordered after every asynchronous user.
Every scratchpad read is initialized; all required group members reach publication and reuse barriers; every logical output has exactly one owner.
Every cross-agent publication uses an observed event or atomic edge at scope containing all communicators; address equality and fences alone are rejected.
Managed placement remains a performance policy, while correctness is capability-checked and independent of residency and migration order with a bounded fallback.
invariant_checking.notes: Checked invariants across allocation, placement, loading, publication, compute, output, transfer/migration, completion, reuse, failure, and deallocation.

evidence: Tile coverage explicitly requires valid global bounds, a declared boundary policy, complete loading, convergent barriers, and non-overlapping output ownership.
Publication proof requires a release/acquire observation or command dependency with adequate scope, rather than accessibility or presumed cache coherence.
Lifetime proof rejects submission as completion, and managed-residency proof rejects pointer stability as physical-location or ordering evidence.
